'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] formally announces that [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] will leave [[Afghanistan]] by [[2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan|September 11]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/04/14/biden-announces-withdrawal-afghanistan-481524 (''Politico'')]
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**Fourteen civilians are killed and four others wounded when the [[minibus]] they are travelling in hits a [[landmine]] in the outskirts of [[Mogadishu]]. A [[Somali Armed Forces|military]] commander blames [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] for the attack. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1842846/world (Arab News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
* This date's notation in [[Calendar_date#Gregorian,_month–day–year_(MDY)|month-day-year]] format appears as the first five digits after the decimal point in the decimal representation of the [[square root of 2]], a famous mathematical constant believed to be the first number ever proven to be [[irrational number|irrational]]. [https://nerdparadise.com/math/reference/2sqrt10000 (Nerd Paradise)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 20 people are killed and three more are wounded after a bus overturns after being hit by a truck in [[Asyut Governorate|Asyut]], [[Egypt]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/14/20-killed-3-injured-when-bus-truck-crash-in-southern-egypt (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Search and rescue|Rescue operations]] commence after the [[SEACOR Holdings|Seacor Marine]] [[lift boat]] [[ship prefix|MV]] ''[[Seacor Power]]'' sinks off the coast of [[Louisiana]], United States. [[United States Coast Guard|Coast Guard]] officials say that six of the crew have been rescued and the remaining twelve are missing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-56742996 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rajasthan]]
*****The [[Government of Rajasthan|government]] announces a 12-hour curfew in all cities from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. from April 16 to 30 due to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/rajasthan-imposes-night-curfew-from-6pm-to-6am-in-all-cities-from-april-1630-101618412021424.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
****[[India]] reports a record 184,372 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 13.9 million. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210414-india-s-covid-19-cases-hit-new-record-as-crowds-mass-at-ganges-for-hindu-festival (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 96 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,987. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/health/coronavirus/2021/04/14/covid-19-bangladesh-reports-96-deaths-highest-count-in-a-day (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****The [[Government of Cambodia|government]] imposes a 14-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in the capital [[Phnom Penh]] and its neighboring [[Takmao]] from midnight until April 28 amidst a community outbreak of COVID-19. [https://m.phnompenhpost.com/national/phnom-penh-placed-two-week-lockdown (''The Phnom Penh Post'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 1,220 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby surpassing 1,000 daily cases for the first time. [https://news.mn/en/795659/ (News.MN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 1,335 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 35,910. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2099703/new-high-for-daily-virus-infections (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Sweden]]
*****The [[Public Health Agency of Sweden]] suspends plans to start using the [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine]] following reports of rare [[blood clot]] cases. 31,000 doses of the vaccine have been delivered to the [[Sweden|country]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-sweden-vaccine/sweden-pauses-plans-for-jj-covid-19-vaccinations-awaits-review-idUSKBN2C11UW (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark]] becomes the first [[Europe]]an country to permanently suspend usage of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]], following weeks of reports that the vaccine may cause [[blood clots]]. The move is expected to delay the country's vaccination program by "several weeks". [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-astrazeneca-vaccine-denmark-stops-use-france-uk-europe/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] receives his second dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. It remains unknown which of Russia's three current vaccines was administered to the president. [https://apnews.com/article/vladimir-putin-immunizations-coronavirus-pandemic-russia-8c2583a7a6b889aafaf5d58a23fa87b0 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports new records of 62,797 cases and 279 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby surpassing four million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-reports-over-62000-covid-19-cases/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yukon]]
*****[[Yukon]] confirms their first two cases of the [[Lineage P.1]] variant that originated in [[Brazil]]. [https://www.yukon-news.com/news/two-new-cases-of-coivd-19-variant-identified-in-territory/ (''Yukon News'')] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/yukon-covid-update-april-13-1.5986347 (CBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
******[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that bars and restaurants in [[New York City]] and  [[New York (state)|the state]] will be allowed to close at midnight beginning on April 19. [https://patch.com/new-york/new-york-city/ny-indoor-dining-curfew-extends-till-midnight-starting-april-19 (Patch.com)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****[[White House COVID-19 Response Team|White House COVID-19 Response Coordinator]] [[Jeff Zients]] says that the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] will accelerate doses of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech]] and [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccines. The move comes after the [[United States]] suspended usage of the [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/14/covid-vaccine-white-house-says-us-is-working-to-accelerate-pfizer-moderna-doses.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The [[Brazilian Senate|Federal Senate]] launches an inquiry into [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]]'s handling of the pandemic, as total deaths are expected to surpass 360,000. Main areas of focus are on allegations that he sabotaged [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic|social distancing]] measures, his poor acquisition of vaccines and touting of ineffective treatments such as [[Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine during the COVID-19 pandemic|chloroquine]], and the cause of oxygen shortages in [[Manaus]]'s hospitals, among others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/14/brazil-senate-investigating-bolsonaro-handling-of-covid-19 (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***In a study published by the [[National Health Service]], the [[Pfizer]] vaccine has been found to reduce hospitalizations in elderly people by 75%. [https://metro.co.uk/2021/04/14/pfizer-vaccine-reduces-elderly-hospital-admissions-for-covid-by-75-14412171/ (''Metro'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] says that it has requested to respond to a [[European Union]] notification of intent to start [[infringement procedure|legal proceedings]] over the UK's alleged breaching of the [[Northern Ireland Protocol]] by mid-May. The UK says that its unilateral delay of the introduction of new [[Irish Sea]] border checks on food, parcels and pets is lawful. [https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-ministers-ask-for-more-time-to-respond-to-protocol-legal-action/ (''Politico.eu'')]
*[[India–Pakistan relations]]
**Intelligence officers from both India and [[Pakistan]] confirm to [[Reuters]] that secret talks were held between the two nations, with the [[United Arab Emirates]] acting as the mediator, in January to help warm relations. Relations between the two had been strained after [[2019 Balakot airstrike|India conducting airstrikes in Balakot]] and [[Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir|India-administered Kashmir was stripped of its autonomy]] in 2019. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-pakistan-peace-exclusive/india-pakistan-held-secret-talks-to-try-to-break-kashmir-impasse-idUSKBN2C12E1?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**A judge lifts the curfew and [[house arrest]] restrictions of two brothers who are suspected of plotting to [[kidnap]] [[Michigan]] Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] last year. However, they are still required to wear GPS tethers. [https://people.com/crime/twin-brothers-suspected-governor-whitmer-kidnapping-plot-released-house-arrest-must-wear-gps-tethers/ (''People'')]
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**The [[government of Sri Lanka|government]] bans eleven [[Islam in Sri Lanka|Islamic]] organizations, including [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] and [[al-Qaeda]], a week before the second anniversary of the bombings after [[Catholic Church in Sri Lanka|the country's Roman Catholics]] threatened massive protests over the government's perceived failure to act against the perpetrators. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/14/sri-lanka-bans-11-muslim-groups-ahead-of-attacks-anniversary (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Pakistani Interior Minster]] [[Sheikh Rasheed Ahmad]] announces the [[far-right]] [[Islamist]] party [[Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan]] will be banned, following days of violent protests by supporters over the arrest of party chief [[Saad Hussain Rizvi]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/14/pakistan-to-ban-far-right-religious-party-after-violent-protest (Al Jazeera)]
